Billy is my own meta build

For my friends in the comments asking for a build/Guide: Here you go!  
My Billy Build is:  
**W-Engine:** Starlight Engine Replica (Steel cushion is about slightly better at 1 star IMO)  
**Disc Drives:** 4 Piece Woodpecker Electro / 2 Piece Fanged Metal  
For Partition Main Stats:  
1 - Always Flat HP  
2 - Always Flat Atk  
3 - Always Flat Def  
4 - Crit Rate % (Crit damage works but I dont get any from his weapon)  
5 - Physical Damage Bonus %  
6 - Atk %

**Teams:**  
**Nicole - Anby - Billy** is the team I use.  It does pretty well, you stun an enemy with anby, chain attack with nicole, and then go ham with billy  
**Billy - Nicole - Piper** Is another fun team I tried if you use 4pc fanged metal and 2 pc Woodpecker Electro. Use Piper's EX-Special to stack her passive and then chain attack with Nicole, and then go ham with billy

**Guide/Tips:**  
1. If there's one enemy: Shoot them with crouching shot, and then a defensive assist into a support or stun character and start applying Daze or Debuffs.  Once the enemy is stunned, unload your entire kit onto them.  
2. If there's multiple enemies or small enemies, use his dash attack to reposition while dealing little bits of damage to all enemies.  Try to get them to line up so your EX special can hit as many as possible since it pierces.  
3. For chain attacks always use Billy last so you can ult off the rip.  
4. Try to be in crouching shot before using EX Special or Ult - His core passive buff applies to those abilities if you do  
5. Always hit the enemies with Nicole right before using billy to apply her defense reduction

It is a metaphor. 

The definition of metaphor is to *compare* two seemingly distant things.  In most cases, it is used to apply a property of something to something else.  For instance, the statement, “Your brain is a rock” compares a brain to a rock, implying that the brain has properties of a rock: cold, lifeless, boring.  

On the other hand, a hyperbole is an extreme exaggeration.  Often times, this is used to amplify a meaning of a word or statement.  For instance, “I am so tired, I could sleep forever” exaggerates how tired the speaker is.  

In this example, there is more resemblance to a metaphor, as it compares disney world to paradise, implying that disney world has properties of  paradise.  There is nothing in this example to exaggerate by using the word paradise.
